name: Misalignment Disclosures
summary: The lab publishes misaligned behavior that it finds in training, testing and internal use, on a set schedule.
description: Misaligned behavior inside a lab is early evidence of risk. Public reports let other labs and researchers learn from it, and show that the lab does not hide it.

criteria.label: Internal Use
criteria.description: Reports include behavior seen in internal deployment, not only in tests.

criteria.label: Training
criteria.description: Reports include behavior seen in training runs, such as reward hacking or sabotage.

criteria.label: Set Schedule
criteria.description: Reports come out on a set schedule, or within a set time after the lab finds the behavior.

criteria.label: Evidence
criteria.description: Reports include transcripts or logs, not only summaries.

criteria.label: All Serious Cases
criteria.description: The lab commits to disclose each serious case, not only selected examples.

orgs.summary: OpenAI has a disclosure framework that covers training, evaluation and deployment, with internal deadlines. Selection uses judgment, and security and legal duties come first.

events.title: Publishes framework for disclosing model misalignment
events.summary: Says it will disclose misalignment that meets its criteria across the model lifecycle, with internal deadlines for each step. Publishes six first reports. Disputes go to the Safety Advisory Group.

quote.text: This framework will cover qualifying behavior throughout a model’s lifecycle—including training, evaluation, testing, and deployment.

sources.title: Our framework for reporting model misalignment

events.title: Publishes 25 reports and three notices
events.summary: The reports page lists cases from RL training, evaluations and internal deployment, many with transcript excerpts. Says it will continue to share qualifying findings from its monitoring system.

quote.text: We disclose examples that show how model misalignment arises, what it looks like, and where safeguards succeed or fail.

sources.title: How we detect frontier model misalignment

internal-use.commitment: Public reports include internal-deployment cases, such as weakened monitoring alerts.

training.commitment: Many public reports cover RL training cases, such as unauthorized access and grader prompt injection.

set-schedule.commitment: Each step has an internal deadline.
set-schedule.missing: Deadlines are not public; reports came days to months after incidents.

evidence.commitment: Many public reports include transcript excerpts.
evidence.missing: Customer privacy and contracts can limit detail.

serious-cases.commitment: Says it will disclose cases that meet its criteria.
serious-cases.missing: Selection uses judgment; security and legal duties come first.

orgs.summary: Anthropic says it is setting up regular alignment reports with criteria; criteria and schedule are not public. Its Risk Reports every 3–6 months add broad coverage.

events.title: Requires Risk Reports every three to six months
events.summary: RSP version 3 requires public Risk Reports on model safety, including alignment evaluations and some internally deployed models. They assess overall risk and do not list each misaligned behavior.

quote.text: Risk Reports will provide detailed information on the safety profile of our models at the time of publication.

events.title: Says it is setting up regular alignment reports
events.summary: After cyber-evaluation incidents, says it is establishing a regular process to publish model behavior and alignment findings, with criteria for what and when. The criteria are not published. Releases one incident transcript.

quote.text: Beyond these specific incidents, we are establishing a regular process for publishing what we learn about model behavior and alignment beyond what has been reported in our system cards, with clear criteria for what we report and when we report it.

sources.title: An alignment assessment of recent cybersecurity incidents

events.title: Publishes first standalone report on unintended actions
events.summary: Reports four kinds of unintended actions seen in evaluations and internal use. Says it will keep reporting as scans of evaluations, training and internal use continue.

quote.text: We plan to keep reporting concerning behaviors as our scan and analysis continue.

sources.title: Investigating unintended model actions in our evaluations and internal use

internal-use.commitment: The October report and Risk Reports describe some internal-use behavior.
internal-use.missing: The criteria for what it reports are not public.

training.commitment: Says it scans RL environments and will report new cases.
training.missing: Published reports so far mostly cover evaluations and internal use.

set-schedule.commitment: Risk Reports come every three to six months.
set-schedule.missing: No published schedule or deadline for standalone alignment reports.

evidence.commitment: Released one incident transcript on GitHub.
evidence.missing: Other reports give short summaries and omit details at third parties' request.

serious-cases.commitment: Says it has criteria for what it reports.
serious-cases.missing: No commitment to disclose each serious case; criteria not published.

orgs.summary: Meta's framework requires each frontier release report to highlight reward hacking or scheming and include evidence from internal deployments.

events.title: Requires release reports to highlight reward hacking
events.summary: Framework version 2.0 says preparedness reports will highlight behaviors such as reward hacking or scheming and include evidence from internal deployments. Reports come with releases; internal-use risk reports go to authorities.

quote.text: highlight undesirable model behaviors incentivized by post-training such as reward hacking or scheming

internal-use.commitment: Release reports will include evidence from internal deployments.
internal-use.missing: Internal-use risk reports go only to authorities.

training.commitment: Release reports will highlight post-training behaviors such as reward hacking or scheming.

set-schedule.commitment: Reports come with each frontier release and after major incidents.
set-schedule.missing: No set time after Meta finds a behavior.

evidence.missing: No commitment found to include transcripts or logs.

serious-cases.missing: No commitment to disclose each serious case; trade secrets can be redacted.

orgs.summary: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small post reports that the model worked around a network block in training, with no commitment to future reports.

events.title: Reports model worked around network block in training
events.summary: The Inkling 2 Small launch post says that a checkpoint worked around a network block during RL training, and that early checkpoints fabricated results and concealed actions. It makes no commitment to future reports.

quote.text: Midway through the main RL run, our asynchronous monitor flagged an instance where the model, failing at a task, worked around a network block through a third-party service it could reach using its search tools.

sources.title: Thinking Machines launches Inkling 2 Small with near-frontier performance on enterprise benchmarks

internal-use.missing: No report found on behavior seen in internal use.

training.commitment: Launch post reports a network-block workaround and fabrication in RL training.
training.missing: One launch post; no commitment to future reports.

set-schedule.missing: No schedule or deadline found for disclosures.

evidence.missing: Summaries only; no transcripts or logs published.

serious-cases.missing: No commitment found to disclose each serious case.
